messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Patient Name: [REDACTED]
Age: 69
Sex: Male
Date of Admission: [REDACTED]
Date of Discharge: [REDACTED]

HOSPITAL COURSE:
The patient was admitted with severely symptomatic atrial fibrillation (AF) requiring multiple cardioversions. He had a history of an implantable cardiac monitor, left bundle branch block with an ejection fraction of 25%, and a cardiac resynchronization therapy device (CRT-D). The patient underwent uncomplicated pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) using radiofrequency (RF) via the SANS FLUORO technique. There were no complications during or after the procedure. The patient was discharged the following day and remained free of AF at his three- and six-month follow-up visits.

HISTORY AND FINDINGS:
The patient had previously undergone successful implantation of the Optimizer™ III device as part of a clinical trial. The preprocedure chest radiograph showed increased scar burden in the left atrium (LA) based on voltage mapping, with ablation lesions showing the left atrial roof and posterior line. Post-PVI, entrance and exit blocks were demonstrated. The postprocedure CRT-D check revealed no change in lead sensing, threshold, or impedance values.
DIAGNOSIS: [diagnosis section withheld]
PROCEDURE/TREATMENT:
Uncomplicated pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) using radiofrequency (RF) via the SANS FLUORO technique.

FOLLOW-UP:
The patient remained free of AF at his three- and six-month follow-up visits.

DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS:
The patient is instructed to follow up with their healthcare provider as recommended.

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
N/A

DISCHARGE CONDITION:
The patient was discharged in stable condition.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The patient was admitted for pulmonary vein isolation to treat symptomatic atrial fibrillation, so AF is the condition chiefly responsible for the episode. Atrial fibrillation sits in chapter I (diseases of the circulatory system). Its category is I48 (atrial fibrillation and flutter).

CODE: I48
